exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong scouting report backs every claim with a rate — here is how one student scouted a swimmer.

traits.sample: Jordan swam 18 laps in 12 minutes, a unit rate of 1.5 laps per minute — the fastest on my list.
traits.why: The rate names both units, so the comparison is fair and precise.

traits.sample: At 1.5 laps per minute, a 20-minute meet projects to 30 laps, so I scaled the ratio 18:12 up to 30:20.
traits.why: The projection comes from equivalent ratios, not a guess.

traits.sample: One 4-lap practice happened when Jordan was sick; it pulls the mean down, so I reported the data with and without it.
traits.why: It identifies the outlier AND shows its effect on the average.

traits.trait: Compares athletes at the same scale
traits.sample: To compare fairly, I put both swimmers at 20 minutes: 30 laps versus 26 laps — now the difference is easy to see.
traits.why: Scaling to a common amount is what makes ratio comparisons valid.
